setup: Sit at a lat pulldown station with thighs secured under the pad and grasp the neutral-grip handles with arms extended overhead.
commonMistakes: Using momentum by leaning back too far
Pulling behind the neck
Not controlling the eccentric

formCues: Lower under control as long as possible
Use hands to catch and push back at the bottom
Keep a straight line from knees to head
setup: Kneel on a pad with ankles anchored firmly by a partner or fixed pad.
commonMistakes: Breaking at the hips instead of the knees
Dropping too fast without control
Anchoring points slipping

setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and hands lightly behind your head.
commonMistakes: Yanking the neck with hands
Using momentum instead of controlled contraction
Not rotating enough to engage obliques

setup: Hang from a pull-up bar with one hand, other arm free or lightly assisting at the wrist.
commonMistakes: Excessive body swing/kipping
Uncontrolled drop at the bottom
Shrugging instead of engaging the lat

setup: Sit in the boat with feet secured in the footplates and oars set at the catch position.
commonMistakes: Pulling with arms before legs finish drive
Rushing the slide recovery
Rounding the lower back

setup: Kneel and place palms on the floor with fingers pointing toward the body, elbows tucked against the abdomen.
commonMistakes: Shifting weight too fast and falling forward
Not engaging core enough to lift legs
Wrists placed incorrectly causing strain

setup: Lie on a bench under a barbell resting on safety pins set at the sticking point height.
commonMistakes: Bouncing the bar off the pins
Flaring elbows too wide
Losing shoulder blade tightness

formCues: Pull toes back gently toward shin
setup: Sit and cross one foot over the opposite knee, grasping the toes with one hand.
commonMistakes: Bouncing into the stretch
Overstretching to the point of pain
Not holding long enough to be effective

formCues: Support lower back with hands if needed
setup: Lie on your back and lift legs overhead, lowering toes toward the floor behind the head.
commonMistakes: Turning the head while in the pose
Forcing feet to the floor with rounded back
Coming out of the pose too abruptly

formCues: Keep weight forward on head, not crushing
setup: Kneel and fold forward, grasping the heels with hands and tucking the head toward the knees.
commonMistakes: Placing too much weight on the top of the head
Forcing the round beyond comfortable range
Neck strain from poor alignment

setup: Sit back in the reclined seat with feet on the pedals and hands on the moving handles.
commonMistakes: Locking knees at extension
Slouching in the seat
Using only the toes to push

formCues: Reach top arm overhead and rotate
setup: Sit with one leg extended to the side and the other bent with the sole against the inner thigh.
commonMistakes: Collapsing the chest instead of rotating
Rounding forward instead of side bending
Rushing into the pose without warming up hips

formCues: Keep torso more upright than normal
setup: Position the safety squat bar across the upper back using the padded yoke and unrack with both hands on the front handles.
commonMistakes: Letting the bar's forward pull collapse the torso
Knees caving inward
Not descending to full depth

formCues: Keep forearms flat on the floor
Reach foot toward head with control
setup: Lie face down, prop up on forearms, then lift the legs and arch to reach a foot toward the head.
commonMistakes: Forcing the backbend before adequate mobility
Letting elbows slide apart
Losing shoulder stability

setup: Sit on a bench with back support, unrack the barbell at shoulder height with an overhand grip.
commonMistakes: Flaring elbows too far forward or back
Overarching the lower back
Not locking out fully overhead

setup: Sit with legs extended or one leg crossed over, spine tall, hand placed behind for support.
commonMistakes: Twisting from the lower back instead of the torso
Slouching during rotation
Forcing the twist beyond comfortable range

formCues: Keep torso still while rotating shoulder
setup: Stand or sit tall with one arm relaxed at the side, ready to circle the shoulder joint through its range.
commonMistakes: Moving too fast to control the range
Shrugging the shoulder up instead of rotating
Compensating with torso movement

formCues: Keep body in a straight line
setup: Lie on your back, swing legs overhead, and use hands to support the lower back as the body lifts vertically.
commonMistakes: Turning the head while inverted
Collapsing through the hips
Placing weight on the neck instead of shoulders

formCues: Hold rear foot with hand for balance
setup: Stand on one leg holding the other foot behind you with the same-side hand.
commonMistakes: Losing balance from insufficient ankle mobility
Letting the knee cave inward
Dropping the rear knee too fast

formCues: Dip knees slightly before driving up
setup: Stand holding a dumbbell at shoulder height in one hand with feet shoulder-width apart.
commonMistakes: Leaning to the side to compensate
Using too much leg drive without arm finish
Pressing the bell out in front instead of overhead

formCues: Keep shoulder pinned to the floor
Stop at a comfortable stretch, not pain
setup: Lie on the side of the shoulder to be stretched with the arm bent at 90 degrees in front of you.
commonMistakes: Letting the shoulder roll forward off the floor
Pressing too aggressively into pain
Poor elbow angle reducing stretch effectiveness

formCues: Extend hips, knees, and ankles explosively
Keep bar close to the body
setup: Stand over the barbell with a wide snatch grip, hips loaded in a partial squat position.
commonMistakes: Bending arms too early
Letting the bar drift away from the body
Insufficient hip extension before the shrug

formCues: Shrug at the top of extension
Keep bar path close to the body
Keep arms straight until the shrug
setup: Stand over the barbell with a wide snatch grip and hips hinged into the pulling position.
commonMistakes: Using arms to pull instead of shrugging
Rounding the back during the pull
Bar drifting forward away from shins

formCues: Take slightly wider stance than normal walking
Use poles for balance if available
setup: Strap into snowshoes over winter boots and begin walking on packed or fresh snow.
commonMistakes: Stepping too narrow and tripping on the shoe frame
Overstriding and losing balance
Not lifting feet enough in deep snow

formCues: Land softly in a squat position
Jump feet in and out together
setup: Start standing with feet together, ready to jump into a wide squat stance.
commonMistakes: Landing with locked knees
Not reaching sufficient squat depth
Poor landing control causing knee valgus

setup: Sit on the floor with legs extended straight out in front, hands placed beside the hips.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back
Letting shoulders creep up toward ears
Locking the knees too forcefully

formCues: Cross one leg behind the other
Lean hips away from the stretched side
setup: Stand and cross the leg to be stretched behind the other, leaning the hips to the opposite side.
commonMistakes: Losing balance during the lean
Bouncing instead of holding steady
Not crossing the leg far enough to feel the stretch

formCues: Keep standing leg strong and stable
setup: Stand on one leg, hinge forward at the hips, and lift the opposite leg toward the ceiling.
commonMistakes: Rounding the spine instead of hinging
Rotating the lifted hip open
Losing balance from insufficient hamstring flexibility

formCues: Explode upward into a wide X shape
setup: Start in a slight squat with arms at the sides, ready to jump explosively upward.
commonMistakes: Landing stiff-legged
Not reaching full extension in the air
Poor landing alignment causing knee stress

formCues: Tap heel lightly to the floor
setup: Stand on a box or step with one leg, the other hanging free ready to lower toward the floor.
commonMistakes: Dropping too fast without control
Letting the knee collapse inward
Using the free leg to push off the floor

formCues: Keep both shoulders on the floor
Let knees fall gently to one side
Turn head opposite the knees if comfortable
setup: Lie on your back, draw the knees up, then let them fall together to one side.
commonMistakes: Forcing shoulders to lift off the floor
Dropping knees too forcefully
Holding tension instead of relaxing into the stretch

formCues: Keep a slight bend at the start
setup: Attach a resistance band behind the knee and stand facing away with a slight bend in the working leg.
commonMistakes: Using hip movement instead of knee extension
Not achieving full lockout
Band tension too high causing form breakdown

formCues: Slide arms under bent knees slowly
Let forehead rest toward the floor
setup: Sit with knees bent, slide arms underneath the thighs, and slowly extend the legs out to the sides.
commonMistakes: Forcing the extension before adequate flexibility
Straining the neck by forcing the forehead down
Rushing the transition into the pose

formCues: Start at a slow, controlled pace
Take shorter strides than forward running
Glance back periodically or use mirrors
setup: Stand facing the console of the treadmill, holding the side rails initially, at a slow belt speed.
commonMistakes: Starting speed too high before adjusting to the movement
Overstriding and losing balance
Not holding the rails when first learning

formCues: Shift body side to side at the top
Keep core tight to control the shift
setup: Hang from a pull-up bar with a wide overhand grip, ready to pull up and traverse side to side at the top.
commonMistakes: Losing height while shifting side to side
Using momentum instead of controlled lateral movement
Not fully engaging the lats during the shift

formCues: Load hips and knees into a quarter squat
Extend fully through hips, knees, ankles
setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, arms ready to swing back before the jump.
commonMistakes: Landing stiff-legged causing joint stress
Not using arm swing for extra power
Insufficient countermovement dip before jumping

formCues: Keep body in a straight line
Lower chest toward the wall with control
Keep elbows at a moderate angle
setup: Stand facing a wall at arm's length, palms flat on the wall at shoulder height.
commonMistakes: Letting hips sag or pike
Not controlling the lowering phase
Placing hands too high or too low on the wall

formCues: Roll open from a side plank position
Lift hips high toward the ceiling
Keep supporting arm strong and stable
Let the head gently drop back if comfortable
setup: Start in a side plank or downward dog transition, rolling the hips open to face upward.
commonMistakes: Collapsing through the supporting shoulder
Sagging the hips instead of lifting them
Rushing the transition and losing balance

formCues: Draw knees gently toward the chest
Keep lower back pressed to the floor
setup: Lie on your back and hug both knees toward the chest with clasped hands.
commonMistakes: Pulling too forcefully causing lower back strain
Lifting the head and neck unnecessarily
Holding breath instead of breathing steadily
